Optima 4: Sequential QP in Depth¶

Sequential QP is the default algorithm of optima(...), and on most smooth constrained problems it is also the one that needs the fewest evaluations. This chapter opens the loop. After it you can read a run iteration by iteration, name the setting that explains what you see, and tell the settings that change the answer from the ones that only change the cost.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

The mental model¶

Each iteration does four things.

  1. Model. Linearize the constraints at the current point and build a quadratic model of the objective whose curvature B is a running estimate (quasi-Newton by default).

  2. Subproblem. Solve that quadratic program for a step d. The subproblem has elastic variables that let the linearized constraints be violated at a price, so it always has a solution even when the linearization is inconsistent. The price is the penalty weight.

  3. Line search. Shorten the step until a merit function, the objective plus the penalty weight times the constraint violation, falls enough.

  4. Repair. If the line search keeps failing, try a second-order correction; if that fails, reset the curvature; if that fails, restore feasibility by minimizing the violation alone.

Decisions¶

Question

Answer

A run ends with flag -6 and the line-search message

Raise max_line_search_iterations; keep initial_step_size at 1.

Many evaluations per iteration

Leave backtracking at 0.5, the cheapest in Program 3 (14 evaluations against 17 and 18), and look at armijo (0.1 took 21).

Equality constraints are curved and progress crawls near the solution

Keep max_second_order_corrections at its default 2.

Thousands of variables

Leave linear_system_solver on Auto; conjugate gradients switch on at the threshold.

The penalty weight seems wrong

It almost never is; read the trace of Program 1.

Pitfalls¶

  • Starving the line search (a budget of one or two trial steps) can look like a solver failure. On the problem of Program 5 it is a configuration failure; Program 3’s problem tolerates it.

  • A smaller initial_step_size looks like caution and is the most expensive setting here: it left one run unconverged after 100 iterations and another stopped with a failure.

  • Tolerances are relative to the problem’s own scale. A flat-looking final iteration is not a reason to loosen them.

Where next¶

Chapter 5 opens the working-set method and the interior method, the two other quadratic-model algorithms, and shows when each beats sequential QP.
